title: Performance-driven Analog Routing via Heterogeneous 3DGNN and Potential Relaxation
problem: Analog routing for circuit performance optimization is time-consuming and requires expertise. ML-based guidance methods suffer from expensive data acquisition and biased predictions.
motivation: Analog routing is critical for circuit performance but currently requires significant development time and specialized design expertise.
method: AnalogFold trains a machine learning model called a heterogeneous 3D graph neural network—which processes 3D circuits where different element types are handled distinctly—to predict how well a circuit will perform after its wiring is physically laid out. To make accurate predictions, it measures distances between circuit elements in a cost-aware way that accounts for actual routing expenses, not just straight-line distance. Finally, it uses an optimization technique called potential relaxation (which improves solutions by gradually loosening constraints) to convert these performance predictions into concrete routing instructions for automatic routers.
key_novelty: It combines a machine learning model that understands 3D circuits with cost-aware distance measurements and an optimization technique called potential relaxation to automatically guide analog routing based on predicted circuit performance.
contributions: Novel ML-driven paradigm for performance-optimized analog routing
Heterogeneous 3DGNN architecture with cost-aware distance for post-layout performance prediction
Pool-assisted potential relaxation method to extract routing guidance
Validation on multiple benchmarks at TSMC 40nm technology node

metrics.other: superior performance compared to cutting-edge methods
